instructions: Rinse the lentils in a sieve. Transfer them to a medium pot, cover with water by 2 to 3 inches and add 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Bring the lentils to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to medium-low, partly cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until they're tender but still hold their shape.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the shallots. Cut the stem off the jalapeño, scrape out the seeds and chop it finely.
In a large bowl, whisk the vinegar, oil, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Stir in the shallots and jalapeño.
Drain the lentils, rinse them under cold water and drain them well.
Add the lentils to the bowl and stir. Leave the salad at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a splash more vinegar.
Serve at room temperature, or refrigerate it for about an hour first. It doesn't need reheating.
method_notes: Food.com and the International Vegetarian Union give the same classic yemiser selatta: brown or green lentils kept firm, tossed while warm-cool with red wine vinegar, oil, shallots and fresh chili, then left to sit for 30 minutes. They call for 8 large shallots and 2 hot chilies; here it's 4 shallots and 1 seeded jalapeño to keep the base mild. Neither version has lemon (the list's note says lemon), so none was added. Neither source has a rating, so this is a fallback lead. The 30 minute rest is on top of the 40 minutes of work, which suits a salad you make ahead and pack.
